_comment: WHERE THE MILLS STAND. Extracted from the WorldData/*.RMB.json block
EACH SUBRECORD PLACES TWO MODELS, not one. WM2d read only the mill and
that is why Mac could see no door and enter nothing: model 118 is a
CLASSIC Daggerfall building - the structure that carries the door - and
the mill (41600) stands beside it. His subrecord headers declare
Num3dObjectRecords 1 while carrying 2, the same hand-edit slip as the
subrecord counts, which is how the second record went unread.
The 41600 record is his own model's placement. The 118 record places a
model the player already owns, at coordinates he chose - so both are
his authorship and neither is Daggerfall's layout.
overrides in Kamer's 'Windmills of Daggerfall' v2.0, vendored with the
author's permission (see README.md).
ONLY THE ADDED RECORD IS HERE, never the blocks themselves. A DFU
WorldData override carries a WHOLE RMB block - Daggerfall's own layout -
and that is game data the doctrine keeps out of this repo. What these
rows are is the placement Kamer CHOSE for his own model: a position, a
rotation, and the subrecord frame it hangs off. His authorship, not
Bethesda's data.
AND THE OVERRIDES PROVE THE MILLS ARE ADDITIONS, which is the question
that stalled WM2b. FARMAA01's file declares NumBlockDataRecords 1 and
contains TWO subrecords; FARMAA00 declares 7 and puts the mill in
subrecord 7. The extra subrecord in each is his. So no classic block
stands a windmill, the port never placed one, and the rotor WM2b wired
had nothing to hang on - which is exactly what Mac saw.
FARMAA09.RMB.json ships ZERO BYTES in the mod while being listed in its
manifest, so that block has no placement here. Six blocks, six mills.
Units are Daggerfall's own, as the block records store them.
